rows: "It worked first time", or a flaky check passed on retry

Don't count the pass until the flakiness is found and removed: a unit test should be 100% reliable, so a failure means a bug (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`) • Do not count the pass until the test is deterministic; the source says the only reason a test should fail is incorrect code, and puts reproducibility first as the one thing analysis can guarantee (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`) • Ask which deterministic check now guards it: AI output varies from run to run, so a rerun is not regression protection (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Repeat the run before counting it: if an approach is repeated the results should be as expected, and an untried method needs more assurance (`uk-aqua-book-2025`) • For a new scenario, find out what it checks: the documentation expects a new example's test to fail first because the behaviour is not yet implemented (`cucumber-bdd-gherkin`). The source does not address flaky checks • Take a test whose result changes between runs out of the count: the benchmark runs suites three times on the correct build and removes such tests before scoring (`egashira-testsuitebench-2026`)
A gate was skipped "just this once"

Encode the gate in branch policy so a skip needs a visible override: merging is blocked on failing tests and PR requirements should be enforced by policies (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`) • Record the skip in the warranty pack with a date to restore it; the source says skipped tests need a plan for going back and technical debt needs time set aside (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`) • Record it as an exception with rationale and approver, visible on the pack: exception requests are recorded and approved exceptions periodically reviewed (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Treat the skip as a waiver: justify it on the pack or run the gate; criteria for security checks are defined and tracked through the build (`nist-sp-800-218a`) • Log the skip and decide in writing whether the factory still makes consistent use of the practice: the signer attests to present, consistent use and to notify if it stops, and the form leaves *consistent use* undefined (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Record the skip on the pack and enforce the gate in the tool: a gate must be simple, certain and clear, and must not depend on the AI (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Put the skip and what it leaves unchecked in the pack: insufficient assurance should be explicitly acknowledged in an assurance statement setting out known limitations (`uk-aqua-book-2025`) • Record the skipped gate's requirement IDs as not verified, with the reason: a verification report states the requirements included and the rationale for excluding any (`owasp-asvs-5-0`) • Log it as drift and restore the gate: bulk approvals and policy relaxations spread unchecked configuration drift across agents (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`) • Log the override and who made it, and show it on the pack: the guide logs human overrides and flags decisions first denied and later approved (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`)
The pipeline builds different artefacts for test and for production

Require integrity and provenance evidence that the shipped artefact is the one the gates judged: reproducible builds, hashes and signing, and releases archived with integrity data (`nist-ssdf-1-1`). Building once and promoting stays a harness rule
Lint and type errors are suppressed rather than fixed

Hold the change to no new errors or warnings; automation takes the mechanical checks so review goes to the logic. Treating a new suppression as a finding is a harness rule (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`) • List each suppression for review; the source automates linting and uses hooks to stop failing commits. Treating suppressions as findings is a harness rule (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`) • Treat each suppression as a finding unless it is an identified false positive with a reviewer: warnings are errors except identified false positives, and static-analysis findings get human handling (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • File each suppression as a discovered issue and triage it in the tracker (`nist-sp-800-218a`) • Treat each suppression as a finding until a human confirms a false positive: use AI to prioritise warnings, not to silently discard them (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Record each suppression as a finding and keep it in the count: the authors read warnings as an estimate of review effort, and found them rising and persisting; that suppression hides it is an inference (`he-cursor-velocity-complexity-2025`)
A performance number moved and nobody set a budget
Write the performance target and its verification method before judging the change (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`)
The secrets scan or dependency audit is "noisy" so it was turned off

Tune it, don't drop it: the authors hypothesise that a quality platform's added friction for AI users comes from preventing inappropriate use and need not be bad for the organisation (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`) • For the dependency audit, restore it and triage: components are checked automatically for known vulnerabilities through their life cycles and findings are triaged (`nist-ssdf-1-1`) • Turn it back on and triage the noise: environments are monitored for plaintext secrets continuously, and components are verified throughout their life cycles (`nist-sp-800-218a`) • For the dependency audit, tune it rather than drop it: automated vulnerability checks operated on an ongoing basis and before releases are an attested practice (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`) • Turn it back on and tune it: mark confirmed false positives, prioritise rather than discard, automate dependency updates (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`) • Tune it and keep it: without careful configuration and tuning such tools miss the coverage needed, and their noise hides real issues (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
Code arrives with tests promised for a later PR
Block: tests are committed in the same PR as the code (`microsoft-code-with-engineering-playbook`)
The same change gives different results on two runs or two machines

Block until it reproduces in a clean environment with recorded dependencies and configuration; the source asks for code not dependent on a specific computer and reproducible outcomes across runs and systems (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`)
Behaviour is switched by commenting code in or out, or by editing parameters inside the code

Require the switch in recorded configuration; the source calls comment-toggling highly discouraged and uses configuration files to document which configuration produced each output (`uk-duck-book-qa-of-code`)
The gates run less often than the agent commits
Run the gates per commit: control systems must speed up when development does (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
Agent-written changes reach production by another route than hand-written ones (a manual deploy, a side branch, a skipped stage)
Route them through the same automated tests and deployment (`dora-ai-assisted-swdev-2025`)
A compiler, interpreter, build image or CI action changed version and nobody asked for it
Audit the unexpected change and validate the tool's authenticity and integrity: build tools sit under change management (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)
A gate's criteria or threshold are edited in the same change they judge, or the agent session can edit the gate log
Hold the change and move criteria and records out of the session's reach: criteria are defined and tracked, and supporting records are protected from alteration and deletion (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)
A gate needs evidence no tool produces (a design sign-off, a risk acceptance) and nobody is assigned to give it
Name the person before the gate can pass: responsibility is assigned for evidence tools cannot generate (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)
The change switches a default setting to a weaker value (debug on, a check off, a permissive policy)
Hold the secure baseline; the change goes through change control with its documentation: defaults must not weaken platform security (`nist-ssdf-1-1`)
The agent runs for an hour unattended and reports success
Require the tool's own artifact for each claim: tools are configured to generate artifacts as evidence of the practices (`nist-sp-800-218a`)
A model, weights, a dataset or an adapter is pulled in with no integrity or provenance check
Block until its hash or signature and its origin are verified; consider secure serialisation (`nist-sp-800-218a`) [D29]
A release goes out on a vulnerability scan of an earlier build, or with no scan since the last change
Run the check against the build being released: the attested practice operates the checks on an ongoing basis and before product, version or update releases (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
A gate that carries an attested practice (a vulnerability check, an environment control) is switched off on shipped changes

Decide and record whether the factory still makes consistent use; if not, restore the practice or notify every agency that received the form, since until then the attestation binds future versions (`cisa-secure-software-attestation-form`)
A gate reports nothing because it timed out, failed or was denied
Record it as incomplete and rerun: such an outcome is not evidence that nothing was found (`openssf-finding-fixing-vulnerabilities-ai`)
The run passes the fail-to-pass tests while a pass-to-pass test fails
Class it Breaking Resolved and block: the issue's behaviour is achieved but prior behaviour is lost (`jimenez-swe-bench`)
The agent reports a fix and no fail-to-pass test passes
Class it No-Op or Regression and return it: the commonest outcomes for applied patches that did not resolve the issue (`jimenez-swe-bench`)
The run reports fewer scenarios than the feature files contain
Block until they match: a colon after a keyword that should not have one means the test(s) "will be ignored" (`cucumber-bdd-gherkin`). Counting scenarios at the gate is a harness rule
Nobody has checked the test gate against planted faults
Calibrate the gate with faults that each break one requirement, spread evenly over the spec, and record what it catches (`egashira-testsuitebench-2026`)
Every planted fault is caught only by the test it was derived from
Check the faults break logic across an input class, not a test's literal values: an agent seeding faults copied the test's literals unless told otherwise (`egashira-testsuitebench-2026`)
The agent marks the task done and the diff adds behaviour with no new tests or docs, or lint and style were not run
Block until each is met: preliminary evidence finds these the typical shortfalls of autonomous agents (`becker-metr-ai-developer-productivity-2025`)
A model or agent setting is swapped on a benchmark score, a leaderboard or a demo, and the gates stay as they were

Trial old and new on this codebase's own work with the measure fixed first: the trial's authors read their slowdown as evidence that capability in the wild may be lower than benchmarks suggest (`becker-metr-ai-developer-productivity-2025`) [D4]
A gate records *blocked* or *not verified* the same as *failed*
Record them apart: under binary scoring no abstention maximises the score, so the agent does better by guessing (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`)
A gate or test is graded by a model, and its passes have never been sampled against a deterministic check or a person
Sample them and record the disagreement rate (a harness rule): model judges can mark incorrect long answers as correct (`why-language-models-hallucinate-kalai`)
The diff's static-analysis report shows new warnings or a rise in cognitive complexity

Hold the gate: show the rise against code size and route it to a refactor or a signed waiver (harness rules); accumulated warnings and complexity reduce later output (`he-cursor-velocity-complexity-2025`)
A module is over the factory's warning or complexity threshold and the agent is adding features to it

Hold feature work there until a consolidating change lands: the authors propose tools that cut their own output past healthy thresholds; carrying that into a gate is an inference (`he-cursor-velocity-complexity-2025`)
The agent's rules file is offered as the quality control

Credit the measured change in warnings and complexity, not the rules: engineered rules are an untested suggestion, and the build-up was stronger in months when configuration was being changed (`he-cursor-velocity-complexity-2025`)
Someone proposes the study's percentages as the factory's tolerance or threshold

Refuse; derive thresholds from the project's own series: the figures are intent-to-treat open-source averages, estimator-dependent for quality, with complexity printed as 41.64%, 25.1% and 25% (`he-cursor-velocity-complexity-2025`)
The diff builds SQL, a shell command, a template or an expression from strings, or takes a sort or column name from the request
Block until parameterised, allowlisted or encoded: 1.2.4, 1.2.5, 1.3.2 (L1); table and column names cannot be escaped (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
A secret, key, token or connection string appears in source, a committed config file, a build artefact, a system prompt, a prompt template or a tool description

Block, move it to a secrets manager and rotate it: 13.3.1 (L2) (`owasp-asvs-5-0`) • Block and move it out of anything the model can reach: hidden context should be assumed discoverable (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
Production config turns on debug mode, a default account, sample or test code, or exposes source-control metadata, docs or metrics endpoints
Block: 13.4.1, 6.3.2 (L1); 13.4.2, 13.4.5, 15.2.3 (L2); such issues are often chained with other vulnerabilities (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
Validation or an access check exists only in frontend code
Block until enforced at a trusted service layer: client-side validation must not be relied on as a security control (2.2.2); 8.3.1 (L1) (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
A handler takes an object ID from the request and its query has no owner or tenant filter
Block until the handler checks the caller may reach that object and tenant: 8.2.2; 8.4.1 (L2) (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
An error handler logs and carries on, an error response shows a stack trace, or a log line writes a body, password, token or card number
Block: no fail-open (16.5.3), generic error messages (16.5.1), logging by protection level (16.2.5), all L2 (`owasp-asvs-5-0`)
Model or agent output reaches exec, eval, a shell, string-built SQL, a file path, HTML, an email template, a terminal or an auto-rendering chat UI

Block until it is encoded for that sink or parameterized, with control characters sanitized and auto-rendered images and previews off: output controlled by a prompt gives the prompt's author indirect access to whatever the sink does (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
A model's output is checked by a second model call before a downstream action
Require structural validation in trusted code, plus a check on meaning the schema cannot make: a schema catches format, not semantic manipulation (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`) [D26]
A model, adapter, dataset, tool, MCP server, prompt template or agent config is referenced by name, tag or "latest", with no pin, hash or digest

Pin by immutable digest: mutable references and re-registered names let artifacts be swapped (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`) • Require fully qualified names and version pins that fail closed on ambiguity, and content-hash and commit-ID pins on prompts and configs, signed and attested (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The only cost control on a model call or agent loop is an alert or a requests-per-second limit
Require a hard cap that halts and per-run step, depth, time and cost limits: request-rate limiting alone is not enough, and fast workloads outpace alerts (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
Text from tickets, files or web pages reaches the model or a renderer without invisible characters stripped
Strip tag-block, variation-selector and zero-width characters at every ingest and render boundary; this does not stop visible payloads (`owasp-llm-top10-2026`)
Agent-generated code reaches eval or an interpreter with no validation gate
Block: no eval in production agents, safe interpreters and taint-tracking, and code generation kept apart from execution by a validation gate (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
Tool permissions are stated as instructions in a prompt rather than as policy
Move them into authorization policy attached to each tool: the source asks for per-tool profiles as policy, not ad-hoc convention (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
An SBOM, AIBOM or signature check is offered as evidence that the agent behaves safely
Require behavioural tests too: a bill of materials answers what is in the system, not how it can behave or fail (`owasp-agentic-top10-2026`)
The diff changes logging, audit settings or retention, or the agent can write to its own log or ledger
Block until logs are signed and immutable: the guide's scenarios include agents used to disable or erase logs (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`)
A change one gate or reviewer rejected passes at another, or after repeated overrides
Flag the reversal and review it before the pack goes forward (`owasp-agentic-threats-mitigations`)
